chunks: (4) Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated from Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa and al-Hasan ibn Dhareef together, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: My father and I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: 'What will you be like when you are in a state where you do not see an Imam of guidance nor a visible scholar? No one will be saved from that confusion except one who prays with the supplication of the drowner.' My father said: 'This is, by Allah, the calamity. What shall we do then, may I be your ransom?' He said: 'When that occurs - and you will not attain it - then hold fast to what is in your hands until the matter becomes clear to you.'

key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: May I be your ransom (a phrase of deep respect)

ai.seo_question: What is the advice of Imam al-Sadiq for the time of the Imam's absence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) foretold the era of the Minor and Major Occultations, describing a period of spiritual disorientation where only those who recite the 'Supplication of the Drowner' (Dua al-Ghaqib) will be saved. He instructed the faithful to cling to the established traditions and knowledge currently in their possession, emphasizing the importance of preserving the foundational teachings until the Imam's reappearance clarifies all matters.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (4) Muhammad bin Hammam narrated from Abdullah bin Ja’far al-Himyari from bin Eessa and al-Husayn bin Dhareef from Hammad bin Eessa that Abdullah bin Sinan had said: My father and I went to Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as).

He said: “What will you do if you become in a time that you do not find an imam of guidance nor any banner and then no one will be saved from that confusion except one, who will pray Allah with the prayer of drowner?” My father said: “By Allah, this is a great calamity. May I die for you! What will we do then?” He said: “If that occurs-and you will not attain it-then keep to that you have had until the matter becomes clear.”
